## Owner-word answers: an answered entry leaves the owner queue, a "later" moves to the later roadmap

In an adopting app the owner answered one entry **Later** and one **Yes** through owner-word issues. By the old
§8.6 the project kept the "later" entry open with `(later: #N)` and re-worded the "yes" entry to list what was left.
Both kept their id with a new text, so an aggregator showed them as changed since the answer and asked again (#93).

- **WORKFLOW §8.6, `rules/AGENTS.md`, `routines/owner-word-wake.md`.** An answered entry leaves the owner queue in
  the settling commit, whatever the answer, and is never re-worded in place.
  - `later`: the item moves to `context/foundation/roadmaps/roadmap-later.md` (a queued roadmap, created on first use)
    as a new item with the next number of that roadmap's own prefix; its backlog entry moves with it. The old row
    becomes `carried (to roadmaps/roadmap-later.md <new ID>, #N)` and the entry is ticked `— later: #N → <new ID>`.
  - `yes`: ticked `— done: #N`. What only the owner can still do becomes a new item of the later roadmap, or a new
    `## Before the next release` step when it gates a release.
- **WORKFLOW §5.1, §12.1, `context_state.py`.** The later roadmap is queued like any other but puts no "start queued
  roadmap" word in the owner queue.
- **Doctor note `owner-entry-put-off`** (not a failure) for an open owner entry that still carries `(later: #N)`.

Adopting apps with an open entry that carries `(later: #N)`: move the item to `roadmaps/roadmap-later.md` as above
and regenerate `context/state.json`.
